newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia Satelindo signs $160 million loan deals.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia Satelindo signs $160 million loan deals.

text.p: Indonesian telecommunications company PT Satelit Palapa Indonesia (Satelindo) on Wednesday signed two loan agreements totalling $160 million.

Satelindo, a unit of diversified Bimantara Citra, said in a statement a $135 million syndicated term loan, from 17 international banks, was arranged by Credit Lyonnais and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and guaranteed by the Export-Import (EXIM) Bank of the United States.
Another loan for $25 million loan was unguaranteed and would come from commercial lenders, Satelindo said.
The funds would be used to refinance costs of Satelindo's Lockheed Martin Atlas II AS launch vehicle.
Satelindo said the $135-million loan has a tenor of almost 10 years. It said commercial lenders will be lending Satelindo $25 million for about five years without EXIM Bank coverage.

Satelindo is 45 percent-owned by PT Bimagraha Telekomindo, 25 percent by Deutsche Telkom's DeTeMobil, Indonesia's state-controlled PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia 22.5 percent and PT Indonesian Satellite Co the rest.
